system.name: DiffDock
system.one_liner: A diffusion generative model over ligand poses (translation, rotation, torsion) for molecular docking, with a confidence model that ranks sampled poses.

content.variant_note: the same protein redrawn three times from t=T to t=0 under a dashed reverse-diffusion arrow, framed by an input, DiffDock, output top line
content.argues: Reverse diffusion turns randomly placed ligand poses into poses gathered in the binding pocket, and the best are ranked with a confidence score.
content.subject: One docking case: a ligand and a protein go in, random poses are denoised into the pocket, two ranked poses come out.

lessons.what_to_learn: Explain an iterative sampler on a real instance: redraw the same 3D object at t=T, a middle step and t=0 at the same position and scale, give each sample its own colour so it can be followed as it converges, and put one dashed arrow with the process name above the row. Frame it with an input, method, output top line in three columns.
lessons.suits: Diffusion or iterative-refinement methods on spatial objects (molecules, poses, 3D structures) where the transformation of one example explains the method best.

evidence: Randomly sampled initial poses are denoised via a reverse diffusion over translational, rotational, and torsional degrees of freedom.
The sampled poses are ranked by the confidence model to produce a final prediction and confidence score.

summary: DiffDock treats molecular docking as generative modelling: a diffusion model over ligand poses, defined on translations, rotations and torsion angles, samples candidate poses that a confidence model then ranks. Figure 1 is a three-column overview on a white ground. The top row reads ligand & protein, an arrow, the small-caps name DiffDock, an arrow, ranked poses & confidence score. Below, the left column shows the ligand's 2D structure above a grey protein surface; the centre shows the same protein three times from t=T to t=0 under a dashed reverse-diffusion arrow, with seven coloured ligand poses scattered at first and gathered in the pocket at the end; the right column shows two pocket close-ups ranked 1 and 2.
summary_zh: DiffDock 把分子对接当作生成问题：在平移、旋转和扭转上做扩散，采样的构象由置信度模型排序。图 1 分三列：左为配体与蛋白，中为 t=T 到 t=0 的三张快照，七个彩色构象渐渐收进口袋，右为排名 1、2 的特写。
notes: Prior labels kept (worked-walkthrough as state-snapshots, stage-pipeline). The figure has no boxes: white ground, bitmaps, text and thin rules. The SVG histogram holds only white, so the palette lists approximate readings of the bitmaps. The 2D ligand structure is a bitmap, not vector (digest: 7 bitmaps, the smallest 67 by 67 pt). The model is only the name DiffDock between two arrows; the confidence model is not drawn.
